William Henry Harrison. The ninth President of the United States, though he served the shortest tenure in presidential history—just thirty-one days before dying of illness. A military officer famous for his victory against Native American forces at Tippecanoe in eighteen eleven, Harrison was elected in eighteen forty as an anti-establishment candidate opposing President Martin Van Buren. His sudden death precipitated the first presidential succession and left the nation with an unelected vice president, John Tyler, who assumed powers unprecedented in American constitutional practice.

Born in Virginia as the son of a Founding Father, Harrison entered the military and became an Indian fighter and territorial governor of the Northwest Territory during the early republic. He commanded U.S. forces at the Battle of Tippecanoe in eighteen eleven in Indiana Territory against a Tecumseh-led confederacy of Native Americans. Though tactically inconclusive, he won popular acclaim as an Indian fighter.

Harrison became a national hero during the War of eighteen twelve, commanding successful campaigns against British forces and their Native American allies. His political career began in the House of Representatives and later he served as minister to Colombia, remaining relatively obscure until the eighteen forty presidential campaign. He was elected president on an anti-Van Buren, anti-executive-power platform. The Anti-Masonic Party supported him, combining with other anti-Democratic forces.

He delivered the longest presidential inaugural address in history, approximately eight thousand four hundred words, despite cold, wet weather without proper clothing. Tradition claims his illness stemmed from this exposure. Harrison died on April fourth, eighteen forty-one, of pneumonia or enteric illness after only thirty-one days in office. His death triggered a constitutional crisis about presidential succession.

John Tyler, his vice president, assumed the full powers of the presidency against the expectations of Congressional Whigs who expected Tyler to serve merely as acting president. As an Indian fighter, Harrison opposed Tecumseh during the War of eighteen twelve.
